transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I haven’t really felt like myself. I stopped doing things I used to do—hiking, coaching, playing guitar. I don’t call people back much. Some days I just sit in my rental for hours, knowing I should get up and do things, but I can’t really make myself start.
How long have you been feeling this way—when did you first notice this loss of interest and difficulty getting started with things?
Probably… a little over a year. It started after I moved into the smaller rental, after the divorce. Maybe a year and two months ago. Things have just kind of been slipping since then.
During this past year, has there been a stretch of at least two weeks where you felt down or empty nearly all day, almost every day, along with things like changes in sleep, appetite, or energy?
I don’t know. I mean… I’ve had bad stretches, yeah, but I’m not sure I’d call it down all day every day for two weeks. Sleep and energy have been… off, but I haven’t really kept track.
Over this past year, would you say you've felt down or 'off' more days than not, even if not severely, or has it been more like distinct episodes with better periods in between?
I’m not really sure. It kind of all blends together. Some days are worse than others, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been keeping track of whether it’s most days or in clear episodes.
Have you had any thoughts that you're worthless, or excessive guilt about things, or any thoughts about death or not wanting to be alive during this past year?

I don’t really know. I’ve felt pretty low about myself sometimes, I guess… but I don’t like thinking about it much. As far as death or not wanting to be alive… I’m not sure. Nothing I want to get into right now.

Thinking about the worst two-week stretch you've had this past year, how many days out of those two weeks did you notice most of these things together—low mood, poor sleep, low appetite, and low energy—happening nearly every day?
I don’t know… I didn’t count it like that. Maybe a few days, maybe more. It’s hard to separate it out. Those weeks kind of blur together.
Over the past year, has there been any stretch of two months or so where you felt back to your normal self, with your energy, interest, and mood returning to how they were before?

No… I don’t think so. Since I moved into that smaller rental after the divorce, things have just kind of been unraveling. That was… a little over a year ago. I can’t really say I’ve had a couple months where I felt like myself again.
Before this past year, had you ever gone through a similar period—days or weeks of feeling this low, low-energy, and withdrawn—at some earlier point in your life?
I’m not sure. I mean… I’ve had rough times before, but I don’t really remember anything quite like this. It’s hard to say.

Was there ever a two-week period in the past year where you felt down, low-energy, and uninterested nearly all day, every day, severely enough that it was hard to function at work or with daily tasks?
I… I’m not sure. There were definitely stretches where things were bad and I wasn’t keeping up well, but saying it was every day for two weeks… I don’t know. I wasn’t really tracking it that closely.
Over the past year, have you noticed a period where you had real trouble concentrating or making even simple decisions, nearly every day, that lasted at least two weeks?
I don’t know… maybe at times. I’ve had trouble keeping my head straight, but I couldn’t really say it was nearly every day for two weeks. I just… I’m not sure.

During the worst point in this past year, was your low mood and low energy severe enough that you had real trouble going to work, maintaining your usual routine, or taking care of basic responsibilities?

Yeah… it got bad enough that I wasn’t really functioning right. I got suspended from my protective service job after an incident on patrol where I scared some staff and people nearby. After that I kind of stopped doing the other things too… coaching, volunteering, being around people who depended on me.

Around the time of that work incident, did you also notice any changes in your appetite or weight, or did you feel unusually restless or, conversely, physically slowed down in a way others might have noticed?

Not so much appetite or weight that I remember. It was more… how I was acting. On patrol I’d react before I could slow down—crouching behind counters, telling people to get back, pacing the same route. I guess people noticed. Staff looked scared.
During that incident on patrol, did it feel like you were reliving or reacting to a specific frightening event from your past, as if it were happening again?
I don’t know. I can’t say it was like some specific past thing happening again. It felt intense, but… I’m not sure how to explain it.

I haven’t really kept track. I don’t think there was a big change like that… not that I noticed.
